messages:
Maria: quick sync — we've had a few tickets & support threads where customers misinterpret 429 vs 503 vs our "degraded" badge. They see a 429 and assume unlimited retries will succeed, or they see a 503 and assume a platform outage. We need consistent client-facing taxonomy + small API fields so SDKs/console can show a single narrative.
AJ: can you paste an example of the confusing payload? any concrete customer logs?
Samir: from support — snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limited",
  "message": "quota exceeded"
}
```
customer saw this, retried aggressively and hit the degraded route which returns 200 + truncated tokens -> worse UX.
Jess: oh that one. UX-wise we should separate "client action" vs "system state". e.g., actionable=hints you can act on (retry, backoff), state describes whether route is degraded vs unavailable.
Maria: exactly — proposal: add two top-level fields to responses we control: `client_action` (enum: `retry_after`, `no_retry`, `use_fallback`) and `route_state` (enum: `healthy`, `degraded`, `unavailable`). Keep `http_code` semantics but don't expect clients to infer intent from code alone.
David: small SDK lift but doable. we'd want backward compatibility so if SDK doesn't parse extras it falls back to current logic. we should attach a telemetry flag so we can measure adoption: `client_status_signal_version=1`.
AJ: telemetry ask: can we emit a topology tag with the response: `route_reason` string and `status_bucket` tag (values: `soft_fail`, `hard_fail`, `retryable`)? that'll let console chart real customer behavior.
Samir: yes, we'll include `status_bucket` in logs and wire to the dashboard. suggests mapping rules:
- 429 with remaining quota > 0 -> `retryable`
- 429 quota exhausted -> `hard_fail`
- 5xx transient -> `retryable`
- 503 node offline -> `hard_fail` / `unavailable`
- 200 but truncated -> `degraded`
Jess: for console copy: instead of raw codes show a single badge + microcopy. Examples:
- badge: "Retryable — try again in a few seconds" when `client_action=retry_after`
- badge: "Degraded — responses may be incomplete" when `route_state=degraded`
- badge: "Unavailable — fall back to alternate region or model" when `route_state=unavailable`
Maria: love that. we should also standardize an SDK-visible `retry_after_seconds` numeric field (nullable) when `client_action=retry_after`.
David: SDKs will honor `retry_after_seconds` over `Retry-After` header if present; safer.
AJ: rollout plan idea: start with hosted API only, canary to 5% of traffic for 48h, then expand if no regressed metrics. Also add an A/B in console where 10% of customers see new badges so we can run a comprehension survey popup.
Samir: telemetry counters we need:
- `client_status_version_seen`
- `status_bucket` distribution
- `client_action` adoption
- conversion metric on support tickets
Jess: copywork for support & docs: update "Understanding Errors" doc + quick cheatsheet:
- what to do on `retryable`
- when to fallback
- how console badges map to behavior
Maria: edgecases: what about Dedicated/Private where customers manage models? we should have the control plane emit the fields but leave responsibility for model-specific messaging to tenant config. propose default to our mapping with override.
David: security: no PII in `route_reason`. keep it short and generic like `soft_throttle`, `capacity_spike`, `model_fallback`.
AJ: ops-bot: deploy queued — canary feature flags ready: `client_status_signal_v1` -> env: prod, target: 5%
ops-bot: deploy started at 2024-05-21T22:14:00Z :rocket:
Maria: next steps: PRs
- runtime: annotate responses + telemetry (Samir)
- sdk: parse fields + expose helpers (David)
- console: badge + docs + A/B hook (Jess)
- product: support communication & survey (AJ)
Can we have PRs by EOD Wednesday? :thumbsup:
Samir: yes, I'll open runtime PR today, include mapping table + unit tests.
David: SDK PR by Weds. Backwards compatible.
Jess: console mockups by tomorrow noon. will add copy variants for A/B.
AJ: I'll draft the support note and the small survey.
Maria: thanks all. if anyone sees a counterexample mapping that breaks a tenant use-case, drop it here. otherwise we'll start the canary once runtime PR lands.
Samir: adding one note — include `route_id` opaque id for debugging (not user-facing) so support can correlate logs.
Maria: good. keep `route_id` in telemetry only, not in client payload. :+1:
AJ: summarizing final API sketch (will be part of runtime PR):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limited",
  "message": "quota exceeded",
  "client_action": "retry_after",
  "retry_after_seconds": 5,
  "route_state": "healthy",
  "status_bucket": "retryable",
  "client_status_signal_version": "1"
}
```
Maria: perfect. logging: include `status_bucket` + `route_reason` + `route_id`. we'll surface aggregated metrics in console.
AJ: ok let's move forward. ping me when runtime PR is up and I'll sync support comms.
ops-bot: deploy finished at 2024-05-21T22:18:03Z — canary gate open for 5% traffic.
Jess: :tada: will post design screenshots in #eng-platform-design after lunch.
Samir: PR opened -> `runtimes: add client_status_signal_v1` link:/pr/789
Maria: closing loop here. thanks everyone. if support sees spike we'll pause canary immediately.
